questions.q: What did people call the Erie Canal project while it was being planned?
How did canal boats climb the 570-foot rise between the Hudson River and Lake Erie?
options: They were carried by wagon between rivers
Through 83 locks that lifted boats like filling bathtubs
They used sails and strong winds

questions.q: Who did much of the digging on the Erie Canal?
options: Thousands of workers with shovels, many of them Irish immigrants

questions.q: How was the news of the canal's opening sent from Buffalo to New York City in about eighty minutes?
options: By cannons firing one after another along the route

questions.q: What happened to the cost of moving freight after the canal opened?
options: It collapsed from about $100 a ton to around $10 or less

questions.q: What did Sequoyah invent for the Cherokee people?
options: A writing system of about eighty-five characters

questions.q: What discovery in 1829 sped up the push to remove the Cherokee from their land?
options: Gold on Cherokee land in Georgia

questions.q: What happened in the Supreme Court case Worcester versus Georgia?
options: The Court refused to hear the case
The Court ordered the Cherokee to move west
The Cherokee won, but Georgia and the president ignored the ruling

questions.q: About how many Cherokee people died on the Trail of Tears?
options: About four thousand, roughly one in four

questions.q: What did the Cherokee do after reaching the west?
options: They rebuilt with a new constitution, a new capital at Tahlequah, schools, and a newspaper
They returned to Georgia within a year

questions.q: How did most people travel the two thousand miles of the Oregon Trail?
Why did wagon trains wait for the grass to green up before leaving?
options: The rivers were too high before then
Their oxen needed grass to eat along the way
The trail was closed in spring
They were waiting for army escorts

questions.q: What was the deadliest danger on the trail?
options: Disease, especially cholera from bad water

questions.q: How did native peoples along the trail most often interact with the wagon trains?
options: As traders, guides, and ferry operators
They attacked nearly every wagon train
They never came near the trail
They charged nothing and gave everything away

questions.q: What did families carve at Independence Rock?
What document did Elizabeth Cady Stanton read at Seneca Falls?
Which famous sentence did the declaration change by two words?
options: Give me liberty or give me death
We the People of the United States
Four score and seven years ago
All men and women are created equal

questions.q: Which demand at the convention was almost voted down?
Who stood up and helped save the voting resolution?
When did the Nineteenth Amendment guarantee American women the vote?
Where did James Marshall first spot gold?
options: In the water ditch of a half-built sawmill
On a beach near San Francisco

questions.q: What did Sam Brannan do before announcing the gold strike in San Francisco?
options: He bought up nearly every pick, pan, and shovel around
He claimed the sawmill for himself

questions.q: What happened to ships in San Francisco Bay in 1848 and 1849?
options: They were turned into gold mines
Crews abandoned them to hunt gold, leaving a forest of masts

questions.q: Who most reliably got rich during the gold rush?
options: The miners with the biggest pans
People selling supplies, food, and clothing to miners

questions.q: What was the gold rush for the native peoples of California?
options: A chance to sell supplies at high prices
A time of new treaties that protected their land
A catastrophe of disease, starvation, and violence
